question: Can full-game likelihood-gradient updates improve a policy when collection and evaluation use the same stochastic execution, rather than a later greedy conversion?
prior_evidence: E36/37 trained complete late suffixes and failed; E183 trained a192-weight greedy whole-policy residual and failed. E188 independent readouts and E190 direct-combat filtering failed on existing data. These do not prove this method works or that whole-policy learning was never tried.
data_gap: E180 found52385 natural map and10318 campfire states with no recorded same-state alternatives. Existing fixed-parent branches and deterministic E183 perturbations are not current stochastic-policy trajectories with their collecting action likelihoods. New complete on-policy outcomes are required for this estimator; old parents still provide initialization, calibration and controls. No new seed search or E133 restart.
actor: Frozen complete parent logits, including first-boss relic preferences and their original finite-action mask, plus f_theta(public original5529 card-context features)-f_initial(features). Copy all1061953 original body/head parameters and train that copy in float64; original parent and f_initial stay frozen. Initial residual exactly zero. No new feature, hidden state, seed or future observation is passed to the scorer.
sampling: Every outside decision consumes one independent Python uniform, separate from all game RNG. Among original finite parent logits, sample softmax(logits/temperature) in both training and evaluation. Roles/index/iteration/repeat assign independent hashed sampling streams; evaluation initial/candidate use the same stream assignment. Greedy original parent remains an additional comparison. No best-of-N winner selection at deployment.
calibration: Before new games, use all outside menus on the first32 assigned historical fitting families. Select the first prescribed dyadic temperature whose mean probability of departing from the complete parent reaches2percent. Use only public logits for this selection; raw terminal outcomes verify old replay, never choose temperature. Replay zero/nonzero adapters, legal actions, public inputs and state/RNG.
learning: At most4 fresh cohorts, each128 fixed old fit families x4 independently sampled complete games. All valid outcomes are kept: Heart1, death/Act3-without-Heart0; no floor or HP reward. Within a family subtract the mean of the other3 episode returns. Apply this advantage to every non-forced decision using clipped importance-ratio gradient plus forward KL to the collecting distribution. Two passes, batch128, AdamW3e-5/1e-5, clip.2, KL.1, gradient norm1. No per-trajectory length normalization. Each complete audited batch is learned before the next batch starts.
stopping: Initial batch needs16 mixed-outcome families; later batches need8. Below this signal check perform no update and stop, retaining the collecting actor. These are stop checks within the precommitted budget, not authorization to expand on finding wins. Keep only the last scheduled actor, no checkpoint choice from evaluation returns.
evaluation: After sealing the final actor,128 disjoint historical evaluation families run both the initial stochastic actor and final actor with shared assigned policy streams. Compare final against each stochastic control and recorded greedy parent. Each comparison needs net>=8/128 and exact paired p<.025. Historical repeated development p-values are descriptive, not proof of final generalization. Passing permits separate prospective validation only.
verification: Verify every recorded public feature, collecting probability, independent sampled choice, game-state/RNG and terminal by native replay. Fresh NN/MCTS and the same policy RNG rerun every stochastic winner. Four fresh greedy controls must reproduce old complete traces. Faults/timeouts stop the study and are never death labels or gradients; retain incomplete artifacts.
constraints: Ironclad A20 to Heart, all keys, two Act3 bosses, Act4; Prismatic Shard excluded. Same engine and MCTS8000/Bossx3/native256-replan guard. No original-game parity work, automatic adoption, changed acceptance seeds or unbounded sampling.
limits: This is a bounded full-game learning experiment on historical families. Different policies across training rounds prevent interpreting raw per-round wins as a matched learning curve. Stochastic policy success differs from greedy success; deploy and evaluate the actual frozen sampling procedure. Auxiliary/optimizer checks do not replace policy gains. Final512/1024 unused-family goal remains unmet.
scope_clarification: The E180 map/campfire coverage figures describe the main E153 training graph. E183 also contains alternative full-game paths, which are retained; deterministic perturbation routes do not supply this current stochastic policy and its collecting likelihoods.
